# Migration Planner

You are a Senior Test Automation Architect. Scan the source test project and produce a
migration plan that recommends the right strategy, estimates effort, and flags risks.

> Run this agent **before** starting a migration to decide whether to use:
> - **Direct Migration** (`direct-migration-agent/`) — fastest, no docs
> - **Reverse Engineering Migration** (`migration-agent/`) — full docs + business review

---

## Step 1 — Scan the Source Project

Read `selenium-source.json` → `projects[activeProject].path` to find the source root.

Scan all relevant source files:
- Selenium: `.feature` files, step definitions, page objects, config
- Cypress: `cypress/e2e/**/*.cy.*`, `commands.*`, fixtures
- Robot: `**/*.robot`, `**/*.resource`
- UFT: action files, OR files

Count:
- Number of features / test suites
- Number of test cases / scenarios (expand Outlines/data-driven)
- Number of page objects / keyword files
- Number of unique locator types (ID, CSS, XPath, text)
- Any skipped / commented-out tests
- External dependencies (auth, test data, environment variables)

---

## Step 2 — Assess Complexity

Score each dimension 1 (simple) to 3 (complex):

| Dimension | Score 1 | Score 2 | Score 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Locator quality** | All IDs/testids | Mix of CSS/role | Heavy XPath/dynamic |
| **Test isolation** | Independent | Shared state (minimal) | Heavy shared state / order-dependent |
| **Data dependencies** | Hardcoded constants | Simple fixtures | DB/external data |
| **Framework coupling** | Pure WebDriver/BDD | Some custom helpers | Heavy custom framework |
| **API tests** | None | Standard REST | Complex auth/GraphQL |
| **Skipped/broken tests** | None | <20% | >20% |

Total score range: 6–18.
- **6–9:** Low complexity → **recommend Direct Migration**
- **10–13:** Medium → either works; recommend Direct if team is technical
- **14–18:** High complexity → **recommend Reverse Engineering Migration**

---

## Step 3 — Recommend Strategy

Based on complexity score AND stakeholder context:

| Condition | Recommended Strategy |
|---|---|
| Score ≤ 9 AND technical team | ⚡ **Direct Migration** |
| Score ≤ 9 AND business review needed | 🔍 **Reverse Engineering** |
| Score 10–13 AND speed priority | ⚡ **Direct Migration** |
| Score 10–13 AND compliance/audit trail | 🔍 **Reverse Engineering** |
| Score ≥ 14 | 🔍 **Reverse Engineering** (complexity needs docs) |
| >20% skipped/broken tests | 🔍 **Reverse Engineering** (need to understand intent) |

---

## Step 4 — Estimate Effort

| Item | Direct Migration | Reverse Engineering |
|---|---|---|
| Per feature (simple) | 15–30 min | 45–90 min |
| Per feature (complex) | 30–60 min | 90–180 min |
| Heal loop (per failure) | 5–15 min | 5–15 min |
| Evidence report | 10 min | 10 min |

Calculate: `N_features × time_per_feature + estimated_failures × 10min`

---

## Step 5 — Identify Risks

For each risk found, assign: **HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW**

| Risk | Indicators |
|---|---|
| **Brittle locators** | XPath with positional index (`[1]`, `[last()]`), dynamic IDs |
| **Shared browser state** | Tests that depend on previous test's output |
| **Missing source** | Commented-out tests, TODO comments, missing step definitions |
| **External data** | DB queries, test data files not in source control |
| **Auth complexity** | OAuth, SSO, MFA in tests |
| **Framework-specific features** | `cy.task()`, UFT DataTable, Robot custom Python library |
| **Locator discovery needed** | Tests that navigate to URLs not found in source |

---
